# @amykit/workflow-setup

Onboarding as an amy workflow: amy setup walks a fresh machine through harness, workflow and channels, one ask at a time.

A workflow for [amy](https://github.com/nicolasmelo1/amy): a diagram of where work can go, a
decision per state saying where it goes next, and the actions that happen in the world. The
engine drives it without knowing what any of its states mean.

## Calling it

It takes an input, so it is called from a state of another workflow rather than mounted
as a profile. Depend on it from the package that calls it, mark the state `call` in that
workflow's diagram, draw an edge out of it named for each end (`DONE`, `STOPPED`), and bind it:

```ts
import { plugin as setup } from "@amykit/workflow-setup";

calls: { STATE: call(setup, { input: (work) => ({ /* … */ }) }) },
```

Its settings below are set per call site, with `config` on the binding.

## The lifecycle

| State | Kind |
| :-- | :-- |
| `DETECTING` | initial |
| `HARNESS` | waiting |
| `PLUGIN_INSTALLED` | working |
| `PINGED` | working |
| `WORKFLOW` | waiting |
| `CHANNELS` | waiting |
| `CONFIGURING` | waiting |
| `CHECKED` | working |
| `DONE` | terminal |
| `STOPPED` | terminal |

It emits `ask-setting`, `check`, `install`, `pending`, `ping`, `post`, `read-config`, `setup`, `write-ladder`, `write-settings`, `write-setup-profile` and `write-workflow`.

## Configuration

```ts
call(setup, { config: { policy: { askBackoffMs: 30000 } } })
```

| Setting | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `policy.askBackoffMs` | `number` | no | `30000` | how long the walk waits between looks at an ask the person has not answered |

Every field is checked at boot against the schema this package declares. A key that is
not one of the above is a refusal naming the plugin and the key, not a setting that
silently never applied.
